drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that one who redeems his consecrated field may borrow and may redeem it partially?
outcomeNote: The baraita's derash on ״ואם גאל יגאל״ supplies the source and the question is settled.

segments.he: וּבְהֶקְדֵּשׁ כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְאִם גָּאֹל יִגְאַל״ — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּוֶה וְגוֹאֵל, וְגוֹאֵל לַחֲצָאִין.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «But with regard to» redeeming a field from «the Temple» treasury, it is permitted to redeem the field in any of these ways. This is a halakha where greater stringency applies with regard to redeeming a field from an ordinary individual than with regard to redeeming it from the Temple treasury. The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? «As the Sages taught» with regard to a verse dealing with one who consecrates his field: «“And if» the one who consecrates the field «will indeed redeem it”» (Leviticus 27:19). The phrase “will indeed redeem” «teaches that» one «may borrow» money «and redeem» his field, «and» one «may partially redeem» his field, despite the fact that one may not do so when redeeming a field from an ordinary individual.
